title: Kolingba Announces Multi-Party Reforms
description: Under domestic and international pressure, President Andre Kolingba announced a transition to multi-party democracy, ending single-party rule under his Rassemblement Democratique Centrafricain. The reforms came amid economic stagnation and growing popular discontent with military governance that had persisted since Kolingba's 1981 coup.

title: Legalization of Opposition Parties
description: The Central African Republic formally legalized opposition political parties, enabling figures like Ange-Felix Patasse and Abel Goumba to organize openly. This marked the beginning of a contested democratic transition period with multiple parties registering ahead of planned elections.

title: Kolingba Annuls Election Results
description: President Kolingba annulled the results of the first round of presidential elections after early returns showed him trailing opposition candidates. The Supreme Court validated the annulment, provoking widespread condemnation from the opposition and international community and delaying the democratic transition by over a year.

title: Patasse Elected President in First Free Elections
description: Ange-Felix Patasse won the Central African Republic's first genuinely contested multi-party presidential election, defeating Kolingba and Goumba. Patasse became the first president from the northern Sara-Kaba ethnic group, a shift from the southern-dominated political establishment that would fuel ethnic tensions throughout his presidency.

title: CFA Franc Devaluation Hits CAR Economy
description: France devalued the CFA franc by 50 percent, severely impacting the Central African Republic's already fragile economy. The devaluation doubled import costs overnight, eroded purchasing power, and deepened poverty, contributing to the social unrest and military dissatisfaction that would plague Patasse's presidency.

title: First Army Mutiny Over Unpaid Wages
description: In April 1996, approximately 200-300 soldiers mutinied in Bangui over months of unpaid wages, triggering street battles between mutineers and the presidential guard. France deployed its 1,400 troops stationed in CAR to restore order, but the mutiny exposed deep fractures within the military and the government's fiscal insolvency.

title: Second and Third Army Mutinies Escalate Crisis
description: A second mutiny erupted in May 1996, followed by a third and most prolonged mutiny beginning on November 15, 1996. The mutineers seized weapons depots and neighborhoods in Bangui, and violence took on ethnic dimensions as soldiers from southern ethnic groups targeted northerners associated with Patasse. Hundreds of civilians were killed in the crossfire.

title: Bangui Agreements and MISAB Peacekeeping Deployment
description: The Bangui Agreements of January 1997 granted amnesty to mutineers and established a government of national unity. An inter-African peacekeeping force (MISAB), composed of troops from Gabon, Chad, Burkina Faso, Mali, Senegal, and Togo with French logistical support, deployed to Bangui to enforce the ceasefire and replace French forces.

title: UN Mission MINURCA Replaces MISAB
description: The United Nations Mission in the Central African Republic (MINURCA) deployed in April 1998, replacing the MISAB force with 1,350 UN peacekeepers. MINURCA supervised legislative elections and helped stabilize Bangui, though armed groups and banditry continued to plague rural areas beyond the capital.

title: Patasse Re-Elected Amid Fraud Allegations
description: Patasse won a second presidential term in September 1999 elections that were marred by allegations of fraud and voter intimidation. MINURCA provided security for the vote, but opposition candidates including Kolingba and Bozize rejected the results. The contested outcome further eroded political legitimacy and deepened factional divisions.

title: Failed Coup Attempt by General Kolingba
description: On May 28, 2001, forces loyal to former President Andre Kolingba attempted a coup against Patasse, briefly seizing the state radio station and army headquarters in Bangui. Libyan troops and Congolese MLC rebels under Jean-Pierre Bemba helped Patasse repel the attackers. The failed coup triggered widespread reprisal killings and displacement of thousands.

title: General Bozize Launches Rebellion from Chad
description: After being dismissed as army chief and narrowly surviving an arrest attempt, General Francois Bozize fled to Chad and launched a rebellion against Patasse in October 2002. His forces, bolstered by Chadian fighters, captured several northern towns before being repelled from Bangui with help from Libyan troops and Bemba's MLC militia.

title: Bozize Seizes Power in Military Coup
description: On March 15, 2003, General Francois Bozize's rebel forces captured Bangui while President Patasse was attending a summit in Niger. Bozize declared himself president, suspended the constitution, and dissolved the National Assembly. The coup was the fifth successful overthrow of government since independence in 1960, continuing CAR's cycle of military seizures of power.

title: UN Deploys BONUCA Political Office
description: Following the coup, the United Nations established the UN Peacebuilding Office in the Central African Republic (BONUCA) to support political transition and promote national reconciliation. The mission worked to organize a national dialogue and prepare for elections, though insecurity persisted in the northern and eastern provinces.

title: Constitutional Referendum Approves New Charter
description: A constitutional referendum in December 2004 approved a new constitution establishing a presidential system with a two-term limit. The charter aimed to legitimize Bozize's rule and set the framework for democratic elections, though opposition groups criticized the process as stage-managed by the military government.

title: Bozize Wins Presidential Election
description: Francois Bozize won the May 2005 presidential election in a second-round runoff against former Prime Minister Martin Ziguele, gaining 64.6% of the vote. International observers described the elections as generally free and fair despite logistical problems, giving Bozize a democratic mandate after his military seizure of power two years earlier.

title: Bush War Erupts in Northwestern Provinces
description: Armed groups including the APRD (Armee Populaire pour la Restauration de la Republique et la Democratie) and UFDR (Union des Forces Democratiques pour le Rassemblement) launched sustained insurgencies in the northwest and northeast. Government forces and allied Chadian troops responded with scorched-earth tactics, burning villages and displacing tens of thousands of civilians.

title: Birao Peace Agreement with UFDR Rebels
description: The government signed a peace agreement with the UFDR rebel group in Birao in April 2007, offering amnesty and integration of fighters into the national army. The agreement was the first of several bilateral deals with armed groups, though implementation was slow and fighting continued sporadically in the northeast.

title: Inclusive Political Dialogue in Bangui
description: A comprehensive Inclusive Political Dialogue held in Bangui in December 2008 brought together the government, armed opposition groups, political parties, and civil society. The talks produced agreements on power-sharing, disarmament, and elections, though many provisions were not implemented and armed groups continued to operate across the country.

title: Lord's Resistance Army Crosses into CAR
description: The Ugandan Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) under Joseph Kony extended its campaign of terror into southeastern CAR, attacking villages, abducting civilians, and killing hundreds. The LRA's cross-border incursions created a new humanitarian crisis in the Haut-Mbomou prefecture, an area already neglected by the central government.

title: CAR Joins Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative
description: The Central African Republic was accepted as a candidate country in the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI), committing to transparency in its diamond and gold mining revenues. Artisanal mining of diamonds and gold remained the country's primary export sector, though most production occurred outside formal channels.

title: Bozize Re-Elected in Disputed Vote
description: Bozize won re-election in January 2011 with 64% of the vote in elections the opposition denounced as fraudulent. Several opposition candidates were barred from running, and irregularities were reported across the country. The contested result further alienated political opponents and armed groups who saw no path to power through elections.

title: Seleka Coalition Launches Rebellion
description: In December 2012, a coalition of predominantly Muslim armed groups from the northeast formed the Seleka (meaning 'alliance' in Sango) and launched a rapid offensive against the Bozize government. Seleka forces captured several major towns within weeks, accusing Bozize of failing to honor previous peace agreements, particularly regarding the integration of former rebels into the army.

title: Seleka Captures Bangui and Ousts Bozize
description: On March 24, 2013, Seleka forces overran Bangui and seized the presidential palace, forcing President Bozize to flee to the Democratic Republic of Congo. Seleka leader Michel Djotodia declared himself president, becoming the first Muslim head of state in the majority-Christian country. The coup plunged the nation into its worst crisis since independence.

title: Seleka Atrocities Trigger Anti-Balaka Mobilization
description: Seleka fighters committed widespread atrocities against Christian and animist communities including murder, rape, and looting, prompting the formation of Anti-balaka (meaning 'invincible') self-defense militias. The Anti-balaka retaliated with mass violence against Muslim civilians, creating a cycle of sectarian bloodshed that displaced over 640,000 people as refugees and 630,000 internally.

title: Kimberley Process Suspends CAR Diamond Exports
description: The Kimberley Process Certification Scheme suspended the Central African Republic's diamond exports in May 2013, citing the inability to maintain chain-of-custody controls during the armed conflict. The suspension cut off a major revenue source, though an estimated 140,000 carats were smuggled through neighboring countries annually during the ban.

title: UN Security Council Authorizes French Operation Sangaris
description: In December 2013, the UN Security Council authorized France to deploy 1,600 troops under Operation Sangaris alongside the African Union's MISCA force to protect civilians and restore security in CAR. French forces moved to disarm combatants in Bangui as sectarian violence between Seleka and Anti-balaka reached crisis levels.

title: Djotodia Resigns Under International Pressure
description: Michel Djotodia resigned as president in January 2014 under intense pressure from regional leaders at an extraordinary ECCAS summit in N'Djamena. He had failed to control Seleka fighters or halt the spiraling violence. Catherine Samba-Panza, the mayor of Bangui, was selected as interim president by the transitional council, becoming CAR's first female head of state.

title: UN Deploys MINUSCA Peacekeeping Mission
description: The United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA) was established on September 15, 2014, absorbing the African Union's MISCA force. With an authorized strength of nearly 12,000 troops and police, MINUSCA became one of the UN's largest peacekeeping operations, tasked with protecting civilians and supporting the political transition.

title: Brazzaville Ceasefire Between Ex-Seleka and Anti-Balaka
description: In July 2014, ex-Seleka factions and Anti-balaka representatives signed a ceasefire agreement in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. The accord called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the creation of a joint monitoring mechanism, though fighting continued in many areas and neither side fully adhered to the agreement's disarmament provisions.

title: Bangui National Forum for Reconciliation
description: A national reconciliation forum held in Bangui in May 2015 brought together over 600 delegates from armed groups, political parties, civil society, and religious leaders. The forum produced a Republican Pact affirming commitments to disarmament, transitional justice, and inclusive governance, though armed groups retained control of roughly 80% of national territory.

title: Partial Lifting of Kimberley Process Diamond Embargo
description: The Kimberley Process partially lifted its suspension on CAR diamond exports in July 2015 under an Operational Framework that permitted exports from designated compliant zones in the southwest. The phased approach aimed to reintegrate artisanal miners into the formal economy while preventing conflict diamonds from reaching international markets.

title: Touadera Elected President
description: Former Prime Minister Faustin-Archange Touadera won the February 2016 presidential runoff election with 62.7% of the vote, defeating Anicet-Georges Dologuele. The election, organized with MINUSCA support, was the first democratic transfer of power since the 2013 crisis and was widely praised as credible by international observers.

title: UN Arms Embargo Partially Lifted
description: The UN Security Council partially eased its arms embargo on CAR in 2017, allowing the government to receive small arms and light weapons to equip its security forces. The adjustment recognized that the national army was severely underequipped compared to armed groups, though human rights organizations warned about accountability gaps in weapons tracking.

title: Russia Deploys Military Instructors and Wagner Operatives
description: Russia obtained a UN Security Council exemption to provide military assistance to CAR, deploying military instructors and private military contractors affiliated with the Wagner Group. Russian operatives quickly expanded their presence beyond training to active combat support and gained influence over mining concessions, marking a significant geopolitical shift in the country.

title: Killing of Russian Journalists Investigating Wagner
description: Three Russian journalists investigating Wagner Group activities in CAR were killed in an ambush in July 2018 near the town of Sibut. The murders drew international attention to the opaque Russian paramilitary presence and raised concerns about accountability for violence against media workers in the country's lawless interior.

title: Khartoum Peace Agreement Signed
description: On February 6, 2019, the CAR government and 14 armed groups signed the Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation (APPR) in Khartoum, brokered by the African Union with Russian and UN support. The accord included provisions for power-sharing, disarmament, and transitional justice, and remains the primary framework for peace efforts despite frequent violations.

title: Special Criminal Court Becomes Operational
description: The Special Criminal Court (SCC), a hybrid tribunal with both national and international judges established by law in 2015, became fully operational in 2019. The court was mandated to investigate and prosecute serious human rights violations and war crimes committed since 2003, representing the first concrete step toward accountability for decades of atrocities.

title: Coalition of Patriots for Change (CPC) Formed
description: After the Constitutional Court barred former President Bozize from running in the December 2020 election due to UN sanctions, Bozize allied with six ex-Seleka and Anti-balaka armed groups to form the Coalition of Patriots for Change (CPC). The coalition launched a military offensive aimed at disrupting the elections and capturing Bangui.

title: Touadera Re-Elected Amid CPC Offensive
description: Touadera won the December 27, 2020 presidential election with 53% of the vote, though only about one-third of registered voters were able to cast ballots due to CPC rebel attacks. The opposition denounced the results as illegitimate, and CPC forces reached the outskirts of Bangui in January 2021 before being repelled by FACA, MINUSCA, Rwandan, and Russian forces.

title: Government Counter-Offensive Recaptures Territory
description: Government forces, backed by Wagner Group fighters and Rwandan troops, launched a counter-offensive that recaptured most major towns from the CPC throughout 2021. The offensive was accompanied by credible reports of extrajudicial killings and abuses against civilians by both Russian mercenaries and government soldiers in recaptured areas.

title: CAR Announces Cryptocurrency Adoption Plans
description: The Central African Republic signaled interest in cryptocurrency as a tool for financial inclusion, culminating in legislation adopted in April 2022 making Bitcoin legal tender alongside the CFA franc. CAR became only the second country after El Salvador to adopt Bitcoin, though the move was criticized as impractical given that less than 15% of the population had internet access.

title: France Ends Operation Sangaris Military Presence
description: France completed the withdrawal of its military forces from the Central African Republic, ending decades of French military presence in its former colony. The departure reflected both French strategic retrenchment from the Sahel region and CAR's pivot toward Russia as its primary security partner, with Russian Wagner operatives filling the vacuum left by French troops.

title: UN Panel Reports Wagner Abuses Against Civilians
description: A UN Panel of Experts report documented systematic human rights abuses by Wagner Group operatives in CAR, including summary executions, torture, and sexual violence against civilians during counter-insurgency operations. The findings intensified international criticism of the government's reliance on Russian paramilitary forces.

title: Constitutional Referendum Removes Term Limits
description: A constitutional referendum held on July 30, 2023 approved a new constitution that removed presidential term limits and extended each term from five to seven years. Opposition parties boycotted the vote, and critics accused Touadera of engineering a path to permanent rule. The government reported 95% approval on low turnout.

title: Special Criminal Court Issues First Conviction
description: The Special Criminal Court issued its first conviction in 2023, sentencing former Anti-balaka commanders for war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the 2013-2014 crisis. The landmark ruling demonstrated the court's capacity to deliver justice, though armed group leaders from all factions still remained largely at liberty.

title: Kimberley Process Fully Lifts Diamond Embargo
description: At its 2024 plenary meeting in Dubai, the Kimberley Process lifted the 11-year embargo on CAR diamond exports, reinstating the country as a full participant in the global diamond trade. Critics warned the decision was premature given that armed groups still controlled mining areas and conflict diamond smuggling remained rampant.

title: Severe Flooding Displaces Thousands Across CAR
description: Severe flooding between January and October 2024 affected over 31,600 people across 18 sub-prefectures, with the worst impacts in Kabo, Bambari, and Birao. The floods destroyed homes and agricultural land, compounding the humanitarian crisis in a country where 3.4 million people already required assistance.

title: Wagner Rebrands as Africa Corps Under Russian MoD
description: Following the death of Wagner Group founder Yevgeny Prigozhin in 2023, Russian paramilitary forces in CAR were reorganized under the Africa Corps structure with closer ties to the Russian Ministry of Defense. The rebranding formalized Russia's military presence while maintaining the same operational footprint in mining areas and counter-insurgency operations.

title: 3R and UPC Armed Groups Disarm in Peace Ceremony
description: In July 2025, the 3R (Retour, Reclamation, Rehabilitation) and UPC (Union pour la Paix en Centrafrique), the two largest remaining rebel groups, disarmed and dissolved in a public ceremony. The landmark disarmament represented the most significant progress toward ending the armed conflict since the 2019 Khartoum agreement.

title: Touadera Wins Third Term in December Elections
description: Faustin-Archange Touadera won a third presidential term in the December 28, 2025 general elections with 76% of the vote, enabled by the 2023 constitutional changes removing term limits. The main opposition bloc boycotted the election, and runner-up Dologuele contested the results before the Constitutional Court, which upheld Touadera's victory in January 2026.
